instruction: WP1 identity unification residuals: (WP1.1) a PeerId or a hash must never become an encryption recipient -- contact recovery must bind the DERIVED public key or refuse the encrypt path; (WP1.2) one write helper for contact identity, so no production call site writes a peer id into a contact's public_key; (WP1.3) every send surface resolves hex and legacy base58 through ONE helper to a single canonical identity; (WP1.4) CRYPTO-01 regression test that a spoofed payload sender_id can never become the delegate's authenticated sender. Tests and greps first; production edits only where a gap is proven on current main.
files_touched: core/src/iron_core.rs (WP1.1 send-path hash-confusion guard made reachable + the wp1_ regression battery; +370/-6)
acceptance: WP1.1: recovery with an unknown peer yields the DERIVED key or the contact cannot be used to encrypt; a PeerId-shaped or hash-shaped recipient is refused, with a real-key control send so the refusal cannot pass vacuously
WP1.1 + restart: real emergency_recover() path binds the derived key (never the peer id) and survives a restart over the same storage
WP1.3: canonical hex and legacy base58 resolve to one PeerId; a nickname resolves to the contact's hex key; that key is asserted genuinely encryptable
WP1.4: the delegate receives the AUTHENTICATED envelope public key plus the canonical identity derived from it, never the plaintext payload sender_id
WP1.2 grep: no production call site stores a peer id as a contact public key

evidence.gap_closed: Commit 6b5b08f3 makes the send path's hash-confusion guard reachable: prepare_message_internal's fast path previously accepted any value ContactManager::get() resolved, and get() falls back to the identity_id -> public_key index, so a stored contact's HASH satisfied "known by public key" and the guard never ran for its own input. The fast path now requires a public-key match (case-insensitive). The identity_id index is untouched for other consumers; a contact still sends by public key; the test now asserts the refusal by outcome plus a real-key control.
evidence.mechanical: $ cargo fmt --all -- --check exit 0; $ python scripts/rules_check.py exit 0
evidence.rule8: core/src/iron_core.rs is outside core/src/{crypto,transport,routing,privacy}; the Rule-8 path gate is not triggered by location. The change is send-path adjacent (it decides which recipient value reaches the X25519 encryptor), so a reviewer should confirm the guard semantics; WP1.4's WASM own-topic half was NOT implemented because the symbol lives in core/src/transport/swarm.rs, a Rule-8 gated path, and remains an open row.

canon_rows.canon_identity: upheld: public-key hex stays the contact addressing key and the write format; this WP removes the paths where a peer id or a hash could be handed to the encryptor as if it were a key. No second contact-address flavor is introduced; base58 is accepted on input and resolved to hex, never stored as the addressing key.
canon_rows.canon_routing_feed: untouched by this WP: no routing entry point is added or changed; the single IronCore::routing_peer_seen entry is unaffected.
canon_rows.instruction_matches: WP1.1, WP1.3, WP1.4 and the WP1.2 grep are met with the four named tests and the zero-match grep above; the extra hash-confusion guard fix is an in-scope proven gap in the same send path. WP1.4's WASM own-topic half is NOT met and is recorded as an open Rule-8-gated row rather than claimed.

not_claimed: The WASM own-topic regression test is not implemented (Rule-8 gated file, needs a non-author APPROVE).
